items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: and bass player named Don Payne who moved to New York

ctx.x: Yes. That was very short. That was three weeks. But he was my first name band affiliation. And there was one chair open on that band and a friend of mine said, “why don’t you try and go on this tour with us, it’ll be a start and you’ll meet some people” and so forth. So it was the fourth tenor chair, and I bought a tenor and I didn’t — I’ve never had an affinity for the tenor. I’ve never even taken the time to find a decent mouthpiece until a few years ago, and then my tenor got run over by a TWA baggage cart and…

was probably nobody that you would know — well maybe there was, Gary Frummer played drums, who later played with Art Pepper and Chet Baker, and bass player named Don Payne who moved to New York and went on to do some Brazilian type things. There was a tenor player, a wonderful tenor player named Charlie Deremal, who had taken Ted Nash’s place with the original Billy May band, and he was a monster. And later for some reason he switched to alto for a while and played lead with Stan Kenton’s band, which I still…
Well you got a little taste of it, you know, big band, you were what 20 years old?
